about: The levels of the patch pyramid from index `from` on are plates of the place, and inside `hold` the first level belongs to them too. ONE BODY: two levels show the same bodies at every scale they share (assets-src/mercury/place/onebody.py, the recipe is plates.json `oneBody`). Outside `hold` (inner, outer, degrees from the spot) the bodies of every plate are the map's own first level reduced into the plate's frame, and only what is finer than the recipe's `fineDeg` is the place's. Inside `hold` the bodies are the place's own at every level, the first one included, so the first level stays in at every distance there and the globe's own relief shading stays out: no body changes places on the way down or up. What changes with the eye's height is the light alone. The levels hold the place's bodies in the hero's light: the first level's own picture above the recipe's widest band, the place's bands under it matched by rank to the hero's bands (to the hero's own crater where the place's first pit lies on it), the hero's colour. tone.png (the square of tilt.json, the same file in both sets, written by onebody.py) holds inside `hold` the place's own picture over that field and outside it the place's low tone over the map's. `tone.height` (radii above the ground, from, to) gives a share G that is 0 above the first and 1 under the second, smooth in the logarithm of the eye's height. The second height lies above the height at which the place's close set has left on the way up (0.17 radii), so the close set leaves over the place's own picture as it arrives over it on the way down, and the ground keeps the place's light until the eye is that high. Inside `deg` (inner, outer, degrees from the spot) the globe draws its own lit ground at G 0 and the level times tone.png times `gain` at G 1, which inside `hold` is the place's own picture as the close view shows it at the handover. Between them the two are mixed by G as powers (each raised by `tone.dark`, the first to the power 1 - G, the second to the power G), so in the dark, well under `dark`, the mix is a straight one. The first height lies just under the eye's height of the judged dive frame 717, so the hold and 717 show the levels in the globe's light alone. `hero` is the hero's ring crater in the place's ground (`at`: degrees from the spot, east and north; `deg`: inner and outer, degrees from `at`; `tint`). Inside it onebody.py (the recipe's `hero`: overDeg, most) takes the hero's light out of tone.png, which is the map's first level over the place's above `overDeg`, divided by `tint` and held to `most`, and lays it into every level exactly as the 8 bits of tone.png take it back. So the level times tone.png is the place's own picture there as outside, the hold shows the hero's crater at the hero's place and size with its rim, its floor and its gold ring, and the dive flies over the same ground. Inside `deg` the globe keeps the level's own colour times `tint` instead of the hue of its curve. It is the hero's light laid into the ground, not a shading from a height field. The crater loses it by the eye's height alone, the same on the way down and up: `hero.height` (radii above the ground, from, to) gives the crater its own share, 0 above the first and 1 under the second, smooth in the logarithm of the height; inside `deg` the globe divides its ground by the hero's light to the power of that share and keeps `tint` by what is left of it. The hero's light is tone.png over `hero.file` (written by onebody.py beside tone.png: the light's file as it stands without the hero's crater, only its square `hero.square`: left, top and size as shares of tone.png's square), both read by the same taps. The first height lies just under the eye's height at the end of the hold, so the hold keeps the hero's crater whole; the second lies above the heights at which the crater fills the picture, so the crater turns while it is small in the picture and stands under it in the place's own light, as the close view shows it. The price, seen beside the approved image: the judged hold frame 615 changes inside `hold` outside the crater, and the place's second pit, which the hero does not have, is gone from the hold. `light` is an option of the globe (thin texels of the level before to a pixel: to, from, power) and null in this state. `tone.warm` is a ceiling on how warm the toned ground may read: where the ground's own colour times the tone picture is redder against its blue than this ratio (red over blue of the colour at luma 1, in light), the colour is thinned toward grey until it meets the ratio, and the brightness is untouched. The tone picture is tan so that the blue grey ground of the levels reads as the place does; the white rims and blobs of the levels have no blue to give, and without the ceiling they read pink under it. It acts by the tone's share alone, so it moves no frame above the first height of `tone.height`.
